titleStmt.title: Posterior parietal cortex: An interface between attention and learning?
titleStmt.author: Bucci

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Posterior parietal cortex: An interface between attention and learning?

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the rat posterior parietal cortex and what it contributes to attention and working memory
span.quote: This review summarizes evidence for and against a role for the rat PPC in attention and working memory and evaluates how the function of the rat PPC compares to that of primates on these dimensions.

span.label: whether the rat PPC is functionally homologous to the primate PPC, and why the behavioural literature disagrees with itself
span.quote: Indeed, the rat PPC has been studied in a variety of functions related to the processing of sensory information, including attention, perception, spatial learning, and working and long-term memory. However, mixed results have often been obtained and the particular contribution of the rat PPC to behavior remains unclear.

span.label: reconciles a contradictory literature by sorting studies according to whether their lesions respected the current definition of PPC and what the task actually demanded, and proposes PPC as an interface between attention and learning
span.quote: Consideration of the specific task demands in the studies that have focused on the PPC as it is currently defined may provide some resolution and explain the apparent contradictory findings regarding the role of the rat PPC in attention.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Several pieces of evidence converge to indicate that PPC may be important for regulating changes in attention that affect learning.

span.label: posterior parietal cortex function in attention and working memory in rats
span.quote: The purpose of this article is to review the evidence for and against the involvement of the rat PPC in various aspects of attention and in working memory.

span.label: review
span.quote: This review summarizes evidence for and against a role for the rat PPC in attention and working memory and evaluates how the function of the rat PPC compares to that of primates on these dimensions.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: PPC serves as the link that converts an increase in attention to a stimulus whose meaning has changed into enhanced subsequent associative learning
span.quote: One role of the PPC may be to link attentional and associative learning mechanisms.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: PPC damage leaves orienting (the attentional response) intact but blocks the translation of that attentional change into learning
span.quote: As indicated in the study by Bucci and Chess (2005) , orienting to a CS whose meaning has changed was unaffected by PPC lesions, but lesioned rats were unable to translate changes in attention to effects on subsequent learning.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: PPC output travels through postrhinal, entorhinal and perirhinal cortex to the hippocampus, giving an anatomical route by which parietal processing shapes learning
span.quote: The anatomical connections between PPC and corticohippocampal pathways in the medial temporal lobe provide a clear pathway through which information processing in PPC may influence learning.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: PPC is recruited specifically when a stimulus loses its predictive validity, which is why it is needed for extradimensional shifts but not for well-learned monitoring
span.quote: The fact that PPC damage impaired discrimination after an extra dimensional shift suggests that it may be involved in attention that is required when the meaning of a stimulus has changed.

span.label: PPC is proposed to link attentional change to associative learning: lesioned rats orient normally to a cue whose meaning changed but cannot convert that into learning
span.quote: One role of the PPC may be to link attentional and associative learning mechanisms. As indicated in the study by Bucci and Chess (2005) , orienting to a CS whose meaning has changed was unaffected by PPC lesions, but lesioned rats were unable to translate changes in attention to effects on subsequent learning.

span.label: the anatomical route is PPC to postrhinal cortex to medial entorhinal cortex, perirhinal cortex and hippocampus
span.quote: Specifically, input from PPC and the retrosplenial cortex converge on the postrhinal cortex. The postrhinal cortex, in turn, is primarily connected with medial regions of entorhinal cortex and discrete areas of the hippocampal formation

span.label: Pearce-Hall: a stimulus captures attention when its meaning surprisingly changes, which then enhances learning about it
span.quote: According to one influential theory ( Pearce & Hall, 1980 ), a CS will capture attention if its meaning surprisingly changes. This increase in attention to the CS enhances subsequent learning about that cue

span.label: removing cholinergic input to PPC impairs learning only in the Surprise condition, leaving the Consistent condition intact
span.quote: Using the task illustrated in Table 1 , removal of cholinergic input to the PPC was shown to selectively impair learning in the Surprise group when the light was paired directly with food ( Bucci, Holland, & Gallagher, 1998 ). Importantly, the lesion did not affect conditioning in the Consistent group.

span.label: a double dissociation: the same cholinergic lesion kills surprise-induced learning but leaves five-choice serial reaction time performance untouched
span.quote: In that study, removal of cholinergic input to the PPC eliminated surprise-induced enhancements in learning, but had no effect on performance when the same rats were tested in the five-choice serial reaction time task.

span.label: immediate-early gene expression rises in PPC when the predictive relationship between stimuli is violated
span.quote: Similarly, a recent study in our laboratory revealed that neural activity is increased in PPC when the predictive relationship between stimuli is violated and attention is increased ( Bucci & MacLeod, 2007 ). In that study, normal rats were trained in the task in Table 1 and sacrificed after one session of the Phase 2 procedures. An increase in immediate-early gene expression (a marker of neural activity) was observed in the PPC of rats in the Surprise group compared to the Consistent group.

span.label: the proposed split: PPC is not needed for attention that guides a well-learned task, but is needed when a stimulus changes meaning
span.quote: The fact that PPC damage impaired discrimination after an extra dimensional shift suggests that it may be involved in attention that is required when the meaning of a stimulus has changed.

span.label: Because the anatomical definition of PPC has varied across studies, results cannot be compared cleanly and firm functional conclusions are hard to draw.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison across the PPC literature: THE REGIONAL BOUNDARIES OF PPC HAVE VARIED ACROSS STUDIES, MAKING IT DIFFICULT TO COMPARE RESULTS AND FURTHER COMPLICATING ATTEMPTS TO DRAW FIRM CONCLUSIONS ABOUT THE FUNCTION OF PPC IN RATS
span.quote: Moreover, the regional boundaries of PPC have varied across studies, making it difficult to compare results and further complicating attempts to draw firm conclusions about the function of PPC in rats.

span.label: Any verdict on rat-primate functional homology for attention is premature given how few studies restricted damage to PPC as currently defined.
span.note: what this limits: the rat-primate homology verdict for attention: DRAWING CONCLUSIONS ABOUT THE FUNCTIONAL HOMOLOGY (OR LACK THEREOF) BETWEEN THE RAT AND PRIMATE PPC WITH REGARD TO ATTENTION MAY BE PREMATURE
span.quote: At this time, drawing conclusions about the functional homology (or lack thereof) between the rat and primate PPC with regard to attention may be premature.

span.label: The evidence base is almost entirely lesion/inactivation work, with very little electrophysiological recording during attentional manipulations.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about PPC activity during attention: THERE IS A PAUCITY OF ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL STUDIES INVESTIGATING NEURAL ACTIVITY IN PPC DURING ATTENTIONAL MANIPULATIONS
span.quote: Moreover, there is a paucity of electrophysiological studies investigating neural activity in PPC during attentional manipulations.

span.label: The review deliberately excludes the spatial learning and navigation literature on PPC.
span.note: what this limits: spatial learning and navigation, excluded by the review: STUDIES INVOLVING SPATIAL LEARNING AND NAVIGATION WILL NOT BE INCLUDED SINCE THEY ARE THE TOPIC OF SEVERAL OTHER ARTICLES IN THIS ISSUE
span.quote: Studies involving spatial learning and navigation will not be included since they are the topic of several other articles in this issue.

span.label: the regional boundaries of PPC have varied across studies, which the review states makes results incomparable
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - cross-study comparison, defeated by a moving boundary
span.quote: Moreover, the regional boundaries of PPC have varied across studies, making it difficult to compare results and further complicating attempts to draw firm conclusions about the function of PPC in rats.

span.label: aspiration and electrolytic lesions cannot separate damage to an area from destruction of fibres of passage
span.note: what this limits: attributing a function to the AREA rather than to what runs through it: THE ASPIRATION AND ELECTROLYTIC TECHNIQUES USED IN THESE STUDIES PREVENT A FUNCTIONAL ROLE FROM BEING ASCRIBED TO A SPECIFIC CORTICAL AREA DISTINCT FROM DESTRUCTION OF FIBERS OF PASSAGE
span.quote: Moreover, the aspiration and electrolytic techniques used in these studies prevent a functional role from being ascribed to a specific cortical area distinct from destruction of fibers of passage.

span.label: many of the informative lesions were not restricted to PPC, so their effects could have come from outside it
span.note: what this limits: the neglect and inattention findings: THOSE STUDIES DID NOT RESTRICT DAMAGE TO PPC AS IT IS CURRENTLY DEFINED, so the symptoms need not come from PPC
span.quote: Indeed, damage that included PPC produced symptoms of contralateral neglect and inattention ( Crowne et al., 1986 ; King & Corwin, 1993 ), but those studies did not restrict damage to PPC as it is currently defined and the effects could have been due to damage outside PPC.

span.label: the rat cannot fixate a central point, so the covert-attention task had to be rebuilt and may not measure the same thing
span.note: what this limits: the rat covert-attention task: EYE MOVEMENT IS ALSO UNRESTRICTED DURING THE PROCEDURE AND RAISES THE ISSUE OF WHETHER OR NOT THE SAME COVERT ATTENTIONAL MECHANISMS ARE BEING MEASURED
span.quote: Eye movement is also unrestricted during the procedure and raises the issue of whether or not the same ‘covert’ attentional mechanisms are being measured.

span.label: a negative homology result may be a failed task translation rather than a real species difference
span.note: what this limits: the negative homology result: ALTHOUGH THE CURRENT DATA MAY INDICATE THAT THE RAT AND PRIMATE PPC DO NOT HAVE SIMILAR ROLES IN COVERT ATTENTIONAL ORIENTING, IT SEEMS HIGHLY LIKELY THAT THE PROCEDURES USED WITH HUMANS AND MONKEY WERE NOT COMPARABLE
span.quote: Thus, although the current data may indicate that the rat and primate PPC do not have similar roles in covert attentional orienting, it seems highly likely that the procedures used with humans and monkey were not comparably reproduced in rats.

span.label: activity in PPC does not establish that PPC is necessary for the task
span.note: what this limits: necessity claims: ACTIVITY IN PPC DOES NOT NECESSARILY INDICATE THAT THE REGION IS ESSENTIAL FOR TASK PERFORMANCE
span.quote: However, activity in PPC does not necessarily indicate that the region is essential for task performance.

span.label: there is a paucity of electrophysiological studies of PPC during attentional manipulation
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[2] · what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - the recording literature that would settle it does not exist
span.quote: Moreover, there is a paucity of electrophysiological studies investigating neural activity in PPC during attentional manipulations.

span.label: the proposed subregions of rat PPC are treated as one area because no functional differences have been described
span.note: what this limits: the treatment of rat PPC as a single area: RECENT STUDIES HAVE BEGUN TO PARCEL THE RAT PPC INTO SUBREGIONS BASED PRIMARILY ON CYTOARCHITECTURAL AND HISTOCHEMICAL DIFFERENCES, and to date few functional differences have been described
span.quote: Recent studies have begun to parcel the rat PPC into subregions based primarily on cytoarchitectural and histochemical differences ( Swanson, 1998 ; Palomero-Gallagher & Zilles, 2004 ; Pérez-Clausell, 1996 ). To date, few (if any) studies have attempted to describe the functional differences between these putative subregions. Thus, for the purpose of this review, the area defined above as PPC will be considered as a whole.

span.label: Posner's covert orienting paradigm, rebuilt for rats - the transfer this review argues may have failed in translation
span.quote: However, the procedural parameters of the tasks used in primates and rodents are necessarily different. For example, the location of the eyes on the rat’s head prevents it from fixating a central point like primates. Instead, in the rat version of this task, subjects must maintain a nosepoke into a central port for set period of time and await presentation of the cues and targets in adjacent ports. The dependent variable is also different in that rats must initiate a movement to withdraw the head out of the center port and then reposition the snout in the target port.

span.label: the Wisconsin Card Sorting task, transferred as a rodent perceptual set-shifting procedure
span.quote: The fact that PPC damage impaired discrimination after an extra dimensional shift suggests that it may be involved in attention that is required when the meaning of a stimulus has changed.

span.label: the Pearce-Hall account of attention as driven by violated prediction, used as the framework for interpreting lesion effects
span.quote: According to one influential theory ( Pearce & Hall, 1980 ), a CS will capture attention if its meaning surprisingly changes. This increase in attention to the CS enhances subsequent learning about that cue

span.label: PPC in rats is defined by thalamic and cortical connectivity plus cytoarchitecture, NOT by function - and the review says the definition changed, earlier studies having used a larger area
span.quote: Identified as a larger area of cortex in earlier studies ( Kolb & Walkey, 1987 ; Krieg, 1946 ), more recent studies ( Chandler et al., 1992 ; Reep et al., 1994 ) have defined this area by its thalamic and cortical connectivity.

span.label: attention is split by this review into two senses with different substrates: attention directing performance on a well-learned task (frontal), and attention engaged when a stimulus changes meaning (parietal)
span.quote: For instance, contemporary learning theories distinguish between attentional processing of stimuli that reliably predict outcomes and guide performance, and attention that is required when a stimulus is an unreliable predictor of future events and new information is acquired

span.label: covert orienting cannot mean the same thing in rat and primate, because the rat version permits eye movement and requires a nosepoke instead of fixation
span.quote: However, the procedural parameters of the tasks used in primates and rodents are necessarily different. For example, the location of the eyes on the rat’s head prevents it from fixating a central point like primates. Instead, in the rat version of this task, subjects must maintain a nosepoke into a central port for set period of time and await presentation of the cues and targets in adjacent ports. The dependent variable is also different in that rats must initiate a movement to withdraw the head out of the center port and then reposition the snout in the target port.

span.label: neglect is characterised as an attentional deficit rather than a sensory one, because it occurs without sensory or motor loss and across modalities
span.quote: Patients with unilateral PPC lesions appear to be unaware or unresponsive to stimuli or events occurring in extrapersonal space contralateral to the site of damage ( Heilman, Watson, & Valenstein, 1993 ). Since neglect occurs in the absence of sensory or motor deficits and involves multiple sensory modalities, it has been characterized as a deficit in attention rather than sensory or perceptual processing per se

span.label: functional homology is treated as an open empirical question distinct from anatomical homology, which is granted
span.quote: The rat and primate PPC have very similar patterns of thalamic and cortical connectivity, suggesting that these areas may also be functional homologues. Yet, the current data do not entirely support the notion that PPC has a similar role in attention or working memory in rodents and primates.

span.label: claim_type: critique
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: mechanism — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Moreover, the regional boundaries of PPC have varied across studies, making it difficult to compare results and further complicating attempts to draw firm conclusions about the function of PPC in rats.

span.label: method: narrative review, triaging behavioural studies by lesion extent relative to the connectivity-based definition of PPC and by task demand
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: review — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Emphasis will be placed on studies that have examined PPC as it has been most recently defined using patterns of thalamic and cortical connectivity in addition to cytoarchitecture.

span.label: phenomenon: attention and its effect on associative learning
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: posterior parietal cortex function in attention and working memory in rats — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: One role of the PPC may be to link attentional and associative learning mechanisms. As indicated in the study by Bucci and Chess (2005) , orienting to a CS whose meaning has changed was unaffected by PPC lesions, but lesioned rats were unable to translate changes in attention to effects on subsequent learning.

span.label: builds-on → Bucci & Chess, 2005; Bucci et al., 1998; Maddux et al., 2007
span.quote: This interpretation is consistent with the associative learning studies that demonstrate a role for PPC in mediating the effects of changes in attention on subsequent learning ( Bucci & Chess, 2005 ; Bucci et al., 1998 ; Maddux et al., 2007 ).

span.label: qualifies → reports of contralateral neglect after posterior cortical lesions in rats
span.quote: Based on these findings and the extent to which lesions were or were not restricted to PPC, it is difficult to conclude that PPC damage in rats necessarily produces neglect like that observed in primates.

span.label: reconciles → the contradictory literature on rat PPC and attention, by task demand
span.quote: Consideration of the specific task demands in the studies that have focused on the PPC as it is currently defined may provide some resolution and explain the apparent contradictory findings regarding the role of the rat PPC in attention.

span.label: qualifies → the inference that rat and primate PPC differ functionally in covert orienting
span.quote: Thus, although the current data may indicate that the rat and primate PPC do not have similar roles in covert attentional orienting, it seems highly likely that the procedures used with humans and monkey were not comparably reproduced in rats.

span.label: supports → a role for PPC in attention required when a stimulus changes meaning
span.quote: The fact that PPC damage impaired discrimination after an extra dimensional shift suggests that it may be involved in attention that is required when the meaning of a stimulus has changed.

span.label: contradicts → a significant role for rat PPC in working memory, particularly non-spatial
span.quote: In summary, most of the studies that have examined a specific role for PPC in working memory, particularly in non-spatial tasks, have produced null results.

span.label: distinguishes-from → the central nucleus of the amygdala, which affects conditioned orienting where PPC does not
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHICH KIND OF ORIENTING, AND THE TWO STRUCTURES ARE ALIKE ON ONE AND DIFFER ON THE OTHER. 'LIKE PPC-LESIONED RATS, THOSE WITH CENTRAL NUCLEUS DAMAGE EXHIBITED NORMAL UNCONDITIONED ORIENTING. However, RE-EMERGENCE OF THE CONDITIONED ORIENTING RESPONSE FOLLOWING REINFORCEMENT WAS IMPAIRED IN CENTRAL NUCLEUS LESIONED RATS, BUT NOT PPC-LESIONED RATS.' A study measuring only unconditioned orienting would find the two lesions equivalent. Q-494.
span.quote: Like PPC-lesioned rats, those with central nucleus damage exhibited normal unconditioned orienting. However, re-emergence of the conditioned orienting response following reinforcement was impaired in central nucleus lesioned rats ( Gallagher et al., 1990 ), but not PPC-lesioned rats ( Bucci & Chess, 2005 ). This suggests that components of the central nucleus-PPC pathway have different roles in mediating changes in attention.

span.label: PPC —causes→ postrhinal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — projects to: input from PPC and retrosplenial cortex converge on postrhinal cortex
span.quote: Specifically, input from PPC and the retrosplenial cortex converge on the postrhinal cortex. The postrhinal cortex, in turn, is primarily connected with medial regions of entorhinal cortex and discrete areas of the hippocampal formation

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · extradimensional shift —contrasted-with→ intradimensional shift
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named neither shift; this sentence names both and states the contrast with its direction - extradimensional is learned MORE SLOWLY. — strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: The fact that PPC damage impaired discrimination after an extra dimensional shift suggests that it may be involved in attention that is required when the meaning of a stimulus has changed.

span.label: PPC —distinct-from→ prefrontal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — a dissociation by task type: attention guiding a well-learned task depends on frontal systems, not PPC
span.quote: Instead, this type of attention has been shown to depend on frontal cortex systems in both rats ( Gill, Sarter, & Givens, 2000 ; Maddux et al., 2007 ; Newman & McGaughy, 2008 ) and primates

span.label: PPC —distinct-from→ central nucleus of the amygdala
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — same pathway, different roles - conditioned orienting is impaired by one and not the other
span.quote: Like PPC-lesioned rats, those with central nucleus damage exhibited normal unconditioned orienting. However, re-emergence of the conditioned orienting response following reinforcement was impaired in central nucleus lesioned rats ( Gallagher et al., 1990 ), but not PPC-lesioned rats ( Bucci & Chess, 2005 ). This suggests that components of the central nucleus-PPC pathway have different roles in mediating changes in attention.

span.label: extradimensional shift —contrasted-with→ intradimensional shift
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS Bucci2009-posterior-parietal-cortex-an-interface-betwe[1]: the relation was always stated, the endpoint names were not in the span.
span.quote: This is referred to as an extradimensional shift and normal subjects tend to learn the discriminations more slowly than the ones associated with an intradimensional shift.

span.label: Reviewing the rat literature, the author concludes that current evidence does not establish that rat PPC serves the same attentional or working-memory functions as primate PPC.
span.quote: Yet, the current data do not entirely support the notion that PPC has a similar role in attention or working memory in rodents and primates.

span.label: PPC damage spares attention that merely guides performance on well-learned monitoring tasks, so the region appears not to be critical for sustained attention.
span.quote: Thus, the available data suggest that PPC may not have a critical role in sustained attention.

span.label: Studies of working memory in rats, especially non-spatial versions, have overwhelmingly failed to find a PPC contribution.
span.quote: In summary, most of the studies that have examined a specific role for PPC in working memory, particularly in non-spatial tasks, have produced null results.

span.label: PPC lesions left orienting responses to a light intact, indicating no deficit in this overt form of attention.
span.quote: In this paradigm, lesions of PPC affected neither unconditioned nor conditioned orienting behavior, suggesting a limited role for PPC in these aspects of attention.

span.label: By contrast, PPC lesions selectively worsened learning after an extradimensional shift while sparing intradimensional performance.
span.quote: Lesions of the PPC exaggerated the normal difficulty in learning produced by the extradimensional shift while leaving performance on the intradimensional shift intact.

span.label: Removing cholinergic input to PPC abolished the surprise-induced enhancement of learning without affecting the consistent control condition.
span.quote: Using the task illustrated in Table 1 , removal of cholinergic input to the PPC was shown to selectively impair learning in the Surprise group when the light was paired directly with food ( Bucci, Holland, & Gallagher, 1998 ).

span.label: Immediate-early gene expression rose in PPC specifically when the predictive relationship between stimuli was violated, showing increased PPC activity during attentional change.
span.quote: An increase in immediate-early gene expression (a marker of neural activity) was observed in the PPC of rats in the Surprise group compared to the Consistent group.

span.label: the regional boundaries of PPC have varied across studies, making results incomparable
span.quote: Moreover, the regional boundaries of PPC have varied across studies, making it difficult to compare results and further complicating attempts to draw firm conclusions about the function of PPC in rats.

span.label: lesions restricted to PPC produced no somatosensory neglect, while larger lesions did produce neglect
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: Ward and Brown (1997) found - THE EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW ATTRIBUTES THE WORK TO SOMEBODY ELSE. The cited name is the subject of a result verb and the sentence carries no first-person marker, so the finding, quantity or definition is the CITED author's rather than this record's. The claim is true and the quote is verbatim - what is wrong is whose result the corpus says it is. Nothing edited, nothing withdrawn: the row is marked so a page can name the source. Where the record is a commentary or review, its `claim_relations` layer usually already names the paper being discussed - the record knows at one layer and forgets at another.
span.quote: Using lesion coordinates that did restrict damage to PPC, Ward and Brown (1997) found no evidence of somatosensory neglect.

span.label: no deficit in covert attentional orienting followed PPC damage in two studies using different definitions of the region
span.quote: In one study, damage was largely restricted to the PPC as currently defined ( Ward & Brown, 1997 ) while the study by Rosner and Mittleman (1996) included the larger area defined as PPC by Kolb and Walkey (1987) . Thus it is unlikely that the null results were merely due to insufficient damage to the PPC.

span.label: PPC damage exaggerated the cost of an extradimensional shift while leaving intradimensional shifts intact
span.quote: The fact that PPC damage impaired discrimination after an extra dimensional shift suggests that it may be involved in attention that is required when the meaning of a stimulus has changed.

span.label: cholinergic denervation of PPC removed surprise-induced learning enhancement but not consistent-condition learning
span.quote: Using the task illustrated in Table 1 , removal of cholinergic input to the PPC was shown to selectively impair learning in the Surprise group when the light was paired directly with food ( Bucci, Holland, & Gallagher, 1998 ). Importantly, the lesion did not affect conditioning in the Consistent group.

span.label: most studies of rat PPC in working memory produced null results
span.quote: In summary, most of the studies that have examined a specific role for PPC in working memory, particularly in non-spatial tasks, have produced null results.

span.label: inactivating PPC mattered only when the task required working memory together with long-term memory
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: The authors found - THE EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW ATTRIBUTES THE WORK TO SOMEBODY ELSE. The cited name is the subject of a result verb and the sentence carries no first-person marker, so the finding, quantity or definition is the CITED author's rather than this record's. The claim is true and the quote is verbatim - what is wrong is whose result the corpus says it is. Nothing edited, nothing withdrawn: the row is marked so a page can name the source. span.quote: The authors found that inactivating the PPC only had an effect when the task demands required both working memory and reliance on long-term memory, but not working memory alone.

span.label: rat and primate PPC have very similar connectivity, yet the functional data do not support homology
span.quote: The rat and primate PPC have very similar patterns of thalamic and cortical connectivity, suggesting that these areas may also be functional homologues. Yet, the current data do not entirely support the notion that PPC has a similar role in attention or working memory in rodents and primates.

span.label: posterior parietal cortex (PPC) in the rat, defined by connectivity
span.term: posterior parietal cortex (PPC) in the rat, defined by connectivity
span.quote: Delimited in this way, the PPC is the area of cortex located approximately 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.5 to 5.0 mm lateral from the midline suture.

span.label: contralateral sensory neglect
span.quote: Contralateral neglect and inattention A hallmark of PPC damage in humans and non-human primates is contralateral sensory neglect. Patients with unilateral PPC lesions appear to be unaware or unresponsive to stimuli or events occurring in extrapersonal space contralateral to the site of damage ( Heilman, Watson, & Valenstein, 1993 ).

span.label: neglect as an attentional rather than sensory deficit
span.term: neglect as an attentional rather than sensory deficit
span.quote: Since neglect occurs in the absence of sensory or motor deficits and involves multiple sensory modalities, it has been characterized as a deficit in attention rather than sensory or perceptual processing per se ( Brain, 1941 ; Critchley, 1949 ; Heilman et al., 1993 ).

span.label: covert orienting of attention (validity effect)
span.quote: Thus, the increased reaction time to the target stimulus on invalid trials compared to valid trials is thought to result from a covert orienting of attention to the side that is opposite the location of the target ( Posner, 1980 ).

span.label: extradimensional shift
span.quote: In the final phase of the task, rats must attend to a new set of stimulus attributes to successfully discriminate between pairs of stimuli (e.g., olfactory dimension instead of visual dimension). This is referred to as an extradimensional shift and normal subjects tend to learn the discriminations more slowly than

span.label: unconditioned orienting (habituation of rearing)
span.quote: Rearing behavior rapidly decreases (habituates) when the cue is not followed by reinforcement (unconditioned orienting), reflecting a decrease in attention to a behaviorally-irrelevant stimulus ( Kaye & Pearce, 1984 ; Gallagher et al., 1990 ; Holland, 1997 ).

span.label: Pearce-Hall attentional principle
span.quote: According to one influential theory ( Pearce & Hall, 1980 ), a CS will capture attention if its meaning surprisingly changes.

span.label: PPC boundaries, as given in section 2
span.term: PPC boundaries, as given in section 2
span.quote: Delimited in this way, the PPC is the area of cortex located approximately 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.5 to 5.0 mm lateral from the midline suture.

span.label: PPC boundaries, as given in the conclusions
span.term: PPC boundaries, as given in the conclusions
span.quote: Defined in this way, the PPC is the cortical region located 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.0 to 5.0 mm lateral from the midline.

span.label: contralateral neglect
span.quote: Patients with unilateral PPC lesions appear to be unaware or unresponsive to stimuli or events occurring in extrapersonal space contralateral to the site of damage ( Heilman, Watson, & Valenstein, 1993 ). Since neglect occurs in the absence of sensory or motor deficits and involves multiple sensory modalities, it has been characterized as a deficit in attention rather than sensory or perceptual processing per se

span.label: reaction time to the target stimulus in the Posner cue-detection task
span.term: reaction time to the target stimulus in the Posner cue-detection task
span.quote: The time between target onset and the behavioral response (i.e., reaction time) serves as the dependent variable and is typically longer when the target appears on the side opposite the cue.

span.label: selective removal of basal forebrain cholinergic projections to PPC or to prefrontal cortex
span.term: selective removal of basal forebrain cholinergic projections to PPC or to prefrontal cortex
span.quote: The lesion consisted of selectively removing only basal forebrain cholinergic projections to either cortical region.

span.label: lesion extent relative to the current definition of PPC
span.term: lesion extent relative to the current definition of PPC
span.quote: Indeed, damage that included PPC produced symptoms of contralateral neglect and inattention ( Crowne et al., 1986 ; King & Corwin, 1993 ), but those studies did not restrict damage to PPC as it is currently defined and the effects could have been due to damage outside PPC.

span.label: task demand: well-learned performance versus changed stimulus meaning
span.term: task demand: well-learned performance versus changed stimulus meaning
span.quote: A commonality between the covert orienting task ( Rosner & Mittleman, 1996 ; Ward & Brown, 1997 ) and the 5-choice serial reaction task ( Maddux et al., 2007 ; Muir et al., 1996 ) is the requirement to monitor several locations and respond when a target stimulus is detected. In both cases, attention is needed to direct performance on a well-learned task, and in both cases, damage to PPC was without effect.

span.label: rearing behaviour as an orienting response
span.term: rearing behaviour as an orienting response
span.quote: Like PPC-lesioned rats, those with central nucleus damage exhibited normal unconditioned orienting. However, re-emergence of the conditioned orienting response following reinforcement was impaired in central nucleus lesioned rats ( Gallagher et al., 1990 ), but not PPC-lesioned rats ( Bucci & Chess, 2005 ). This suggests that components of the central nucleus-PPC pathway have different roles in mediating changes in attention.

span.label: 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.0 to 5.0 mm lateral — Stereotaxic boundaries of the rat posterior parietal cortex as the review defines it, on which the whole comparison of studies rests
span.quote: Defined in this way, the PPC is the cortical region located 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.0 to 5.0 mm lateral from the midline.

span.label: 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.5 to 5.0 mm lateral — the PPC boundary as stated in section 2.1, attributed to Chandler 1992 and Reep 1994
span.quote: Delimited in this way, the PPC is the area of cortex located approximately 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.5 to 5.0 mm lateral from the midline suture.

span.label: 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.0 to 5.0 mm lateral — the PPC boundary as stated in the conclusions, attributed to the SAME two sources - the lateral extent differs by 0.5 mm from the value given earlier in the same paper
span.quote: Defined in this way, the PPC is the cortical region located 3.5 to 5.0 mm posterior to bregma and 1.0 to 5.0 mm lateral from the midline.

span.label: immediate-early gene expression
span.quote: Similarly, a recent study in our laboratory revealed that neural activity is increased in PPC when the predictive relationship between stimuli is violated and attention is increased ( Bucci & MacLeod, 2007 ). In that study, normal rats were trained in the task in Table 1 and sacrificed after one session of the Phase 2 procedures. An increase in immediate-early gene expression (a marker of neural activity) was observed in the PPC of rats in the Surprise group compared to the Consistent group.
